mostImportantThingInThisReview: The row was compiled on a premise that measurement does not support in the direction it feared: the copy that could strand (LDT's atoms secret) is consumed by NOTHING in either project, while every consumed staging secret is already a rotation target whose written value is byte-stable on the restore path -- so the disjunction holds today by identity AND by target-hood. The deliverable is therefore not a fix but a STANDING measurement: a check that reads the consumer list from the services' own configuration, fails hard when a consumed secret is neither a target nor identical to one, refuses when it cannot read, and was observed failing on live data before it was trusted. The one thing the row asked for that this lane refused is the third rotation target, and it refused on measured IAM grounds rather than preference: adding it would make every staging-reset fail closed.
